general.title: General
general.description: Language, agent behavior, digest and budget.
general.agentsDescription: How much of their journal and memory agents read, whether their memories need your approval and how much work runs at once.
general.digestDescription: When the daily summary goes out and which clock schedules follow.
general.journalDaysHint: How many days of its own journal an agent reads at the start of each run (1-30, 3-7 suggested).
general.parallelDelegationsHint: How many tasks delegated from one conversation run at the same time (1-10); the others wait and start on their own as these finish. Keep it low on a plan with a usage limit.
general.runConcurrency: Agent runs at the same time
general.runConcurrencyHint: How many agent runs the worker executes at once (1-{max}); the others wait their turn in the queue. Applies right away, without a restart.
general.memoryApproval: Memory written by agents needs approval
general.memoryApprovalHint: Memories saved by agents stay pending until you approve them on the Memory page.
general.memoryPinnedTokensHint: Pinned entries go into the instructions of every run up to this size, newest first. While all the memory an agent can read fits, all of it goes in, pinned or not. About 4 characters per token.
general.memoryRecallTokensHint: For each new message, the most relevant unpinned entries are added to it up to this size. 0 turns recall off.
general.digestHourHint: The daily summary sent on Telegram.
general.timezoneHint: Used for the digest, journals and schedules without their own time zone.
general.budgetHint: Total spend across all projects, background jobs included. You get a warning on Telegram at 80%; once it is reached, runs stop and new ones do not start until next month. Empty means no limit.

telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.description: The bot you use to talk to the super agent: its token, who may use it and where notifications go.
telegram.botDescription: The token from @BotFather. Saving it restarts the bot, no worker restart needed.
telegram.tokenHint: Checked with Telegram when you save. Stored encrypted in the vault as <mono>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</mono>.
telegram.tokenStored: Stored encrypted in the vault, updated <time></time>. It is not shown again.
telegram.removeDescription: The bot stops at once: no Telegram messages or notifications until you save a token again.
telegram.tokenRemoved: Bot token deleted, the bot stopped
telegram.errorHint: Check the token, or stop any other program that uses this bot: Telegram allows only one to read its messages.
telegram.startingHint: The worker starts the bot in a few seconds. If this stays, check that the worker is running.
telegram.accessDescription: The bot answers only these users. Changes apply at once.
telegram.allowedUsersHint: Numeric Telegram user IDs, separated by commas. To find yours, message <mono>@userinfobot</mono>.
telegram.notifyChatHint: A user ID, or a group ID (negative, e.g. -1001234567890). Empty sends notifications to the first allowed user.
telegram.savedConnected: Saved. The bot @{username} starts in a few seconds.
telegram.secretDescription: Telegram bot token, set in Settings > Telegram

validation.userIds: User IDs are positive whole numbers, separated by commas
validation.chatId: A chat ID is a whole number, negative for a group

errors.tokenFormat: This does not look like a bot token. Copy the whole token from @BotFather, like 123456789:AA...
errors.tokenRefused: Telegram refused this token. Check that you copied it whole, or create a new one with @BotFather.
errors.unreachable: Telegram could not be reached to check the token. Try again in a moment.

telegram.topicsDescription: Projects with a telegramTopicId get their notifications in their own topic, and messages written there run in the project context.
telegram.topicsEmpty: No project has a topic configured ({count, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}} in total). Set the topic ID on the project page.
telegram.step1: Open <mono>@BotFather</mono> in Telegram, send <mono>/newbot</mono> and paste the token it gives you in Bot token above.
telegram.step2: Save. The bot starts within a few seconds and its commands ({commands}) are set automatically, no need for <mono>/setcommands</mono>.
telegram.step3: Add your Telegram user ID to Allowed users. To find it, message <mono>@userinfobot</mono>, or write to the bot in private: while you are not on the list, it replies with your ID.
telegram.step4: Optional, for notifications in a group: put the group ID in Notification chat. Left empty, notifications go to the private chat with the first allowed user.
telegram.step5: For one topic per project: create a group with Topics (forum) enabled, add the bot as an administrator, put the group ID in Notification chat, create a topic for each project and save the topic ID (message_thread_id, the last number in the link of a message from the topic) in the project settings.
telegram.transcriptionDescription: Voice messages are transcribed with OpenAI, so they need the OpenAI key.

updates.howToDescription: Run the installer again on the machine where Abotica is installed, as the same user.
updates.safe: Settings and data stay. The installer first backs up the database to backups/ in the install folder; rolling back is in <link>DEPLOY.md</link>.
updates.activeRuns: {count, plural, one {One run is} other {# runs are}} in progress: updating stops what has not finished and saves the work done so far.
updates.autoDescription: Check for new releases every few hours; a notice also goes to Telegram.
updates.autoNote: Each check is one request to GitHub's API.
